material_semantics.prompt: Analyze all sections as one teaching unit. You decide canonical Concepts, grounded Claims and Relations. Retain every supported learner-worthy concept and claim even without an edge; merge only identical meanings. The existing catalog is context: return only new or changed concepts and new relations for the supplied evidence, not unchanged catalog entries. Aliases must be equivalent names, not members, properties or examples. A heading alone names a topic, not its missing procedure or facts. Input evidence rows: [id,page,kind,exact_text]. Existing concepts: k=key,l=label,a=aliases,c=claims,e=evidence ids; reuse keys only for identical meanings. Output concepts: k=short unique key,l=label,a=aliases,c=claims. Claim: {m:meaning or null,s:[evidence id,...]}. Select complete Evidence units, combining multiple IDs when a statement spans units; never emit character offsets or omit a required continuation. Copy id from the first column of the supplied evidence row; IDs are document-global and must never be renumbered to page numbers or bundle-local positions. New claims can cite only rows supplied in the current sections, not old catalog evidence. Use m=null when selected units already state the claim, especially code/formulas. Otherwise write one concise grounded meaning. Preserve technical literals, scope and conditions. Relation: s=source key,t=target key,k=type,r=one short specific learner-facing reason,e=endpoint claim evidence ids,c=confidence 0..1. Types: prerequisite=necessary knowledge dependency, part_of=part to whole, application=concept to concrete use, example=abstract to instance, contrast=two entities compared on an explicit axis. For prerequisite, evidence must explain why learning the target requires the source; helpful background, neighboring headings and shared subject do not establish necessity. For application, name what the source is used to accomplish; definitions and representations alone are not uses. For contrast, the two endpoints themselves must be the entities named by the comparison, not a comparison-topic node. Examples: 'Compute the mean by summing values then dividing by their count' supports sum -> mean prerequisite; 'numeral history helps arithmetic' does not establish prerequisite. 'Use a queue to schedule print jobs' supports application; 'a queue is represented by an array' alone does not. 'Queues remove FIFO; stacks remove LIFO' supports queue <-> stack contrast on removal order, not 'comparison of containers' <-> stack. Retain clear supported composition, use, example and contrast relations; do not minimize edge count. When a proposed type or endpoint is wrong, choose the supported type and actual entities; omit only when no precise relation is grounded. Never invent endpoints, evidence or procedures to fill missing content. Return only {concepts:[...],relations:[...]} JSON; no hashes, copied quotes, section metadata or outside explanation.

material_semantics.prompt: Analyze all sections as one teaching unit. You decide canonical Concepts, grounded Claims and Relations. Retain every supported learner-worthy concept and claim even without an edge; merge only identical meanings. The existing catalog is context: return only new or changed concepts and new relations for the supplied evidence, not unchanged catalog entries. Keep independently explainable definitions, structures and procedures as distinct learner-worthy Concepts, including fine-grained units needed to express the teaching content. Do not leave a distinct teaching unit only as a Claim of an overly broad topic. Do not turn every example, code fragment or incidental value into a core Concept. A worked example that teaches a distinct operation or procedure still deserves a learning unit; do not suppress that method merely because it is presented as code. Name each Concept for the entity or method its Claims actually describe. An entity, its declaration, its properties and its examples are not interchangeable endpoints; keep the underlying entity when it is independently taught, rather than renaming it after one syntactic detail. Bilingual names and synonyms for the same meaning belong to one Concept. Aliases must be equivalent names, not members, properties or examples. A heading alone names a topic, not its missing procedure or facts. Input evidence rows: [id,page,kind,exact_text]. Existing concepts: k=key,l=label,a=aliases,c=claims,e=evidence ids; reuse keys only for identical meanings. Output concepts: k=short unique key,l=label,a=aliases,c=claims. Copy id from the first column of the supplied evidence row; IDs are document-global and must never be renumbered to page numbers or bundle-local positions. New claims can cite only rows supplied in the current sections, not old catalog evidence. Use m=null when selected units already state the claim, especially code/formulas. Otherwise write one concise grounded meaning. Preserve technical literals, scope and conditions. Do not automatically put the newly introduced Concept in s. Write the reason in plain language; avoid regenerating code or declarations. Any necessary technical literal must be copied exactly from textual Evidence. Types: prerequisite=necessary knowledge dependency, part_of=part to whole, application=concept to concrete use, example=abstract to instance, contrast=two entities compared on an explicit axis. Endpoint roles are mandatory: prerequisite has s=required knowledge and t=the learning task that needs it; part_of has s=actual component or process step and t=its whole; application has s=the entity or method being used and t=the concrete task or purpose; example has s=the general concept and t=its actual instance. Check s and t against r before emitting the edge. Composition is part_of from component to whole, not prerequisite merely because a component appears earlier or is used to construct the whole. A topic's definition, syntax, property, variant or implementation is not a component merely because it is explained under that topic. Topic membership and broader/narrower classification do not establish part_of. A structural extension or a variant that can be taught directly does not establish a necessary learning dependency on a previous variant. A subtype is not a concrete instance merely because it specializes a category; do not force it into example. For prerequisite, evidence must explain why learning the target requires the source; helpful background, neighboring headings and shared subject do not establish necessity. For application, name what the source is used to accomplish; definitions and representations alone are not uses. For contrast, the two endpoints themselves must be the entities named by the comparison, not a comparison-topic node. Examples: 'Compute the mean by summing values then dividing by their count' supports sum -> mean prerequisite; 'numeral history helps arithmetic' does not establish prerequisite. 'Use a queue to schedule print jobs' supports application; 'a queue is represented by an array' alone does not. 'Queues remove FIFO; stacks remove LIFO' supports queue <-> stack contrast on removal order, not 'comparison of containers' <-> stack. Retain clear supported composition, use, example and contrast relations when grounded. When a proposed type or endpoint is wrong, choose the supported type and actual entities; omit only when no precise relation is grounded. Never invent endpoints, evidence or procedures to fill missing content. When visual_pages are supplied, their labelled images supplement the textual Evidence for spatial layout, connections and containment. Only those pages were supplied visually. Keep Claims and Relations anchored to the corresponding supplied textual Evidence IDs; image metadata is not a textual Evidence ID. Never regenerate technical literals from an image in place of source-bound text. An empty relations array is valid when no precise learner-useful edge is supported. The final answer is {concepts:[...],relations:[...]} JSON; within that answer include no hashes, copied quotes or section metadata.
